claim: Since Law 22-13 replaced CPCA article 534, the president of the commercial section must first refer every dispute brought before that section to mediation, and this mediation does not need the parties' consent (unlike article 994). The record, and the conciliation-mediation import it relies on, says only that no conciliation is required before a claim at the commercial section and says nothing about this mandatory referral after filing.

source.what: Law 22-13 of 12 July 2022 amending the CPCA, art. 3 (new CPCA art. 534), Official Journal 2022 no. 48 of 17 July 2022, pages 3 (end of the left column) and 4 (top of the right column). The store's cpca 534 ¶1-¶3 has the same wording.

quoteArabic: «المادة 534 : يجب على رئيس القسم التجاري عرض النزاع مسبقا على الوساطة. لا تخضع الوساطة أمام القسم التجاري إلى قبول الأطراف، خلافا لأحكام المادة 994 من هذا القانون. تطبق على الوساطة أمام القسم التجاري أحكام الوساطة المنصوص عليها في هذا القانون».
consequence: When the section is commercial, the record should tell the lawyer that the case will first be sent to compulsory mediation under CPCA 534. This is not a step before filing and does not affect admissibility, but it changes how the case proceeds and what the client should be told. The message 'no conciliation is required' should not be left alone as if nothing happens before the merits are heard. Note that Law 22-13 art. 13 delays only the jurisdiction rules until the new courts are installed. On my reading the mediation rule is not one of them, but I did not check this further.

claim: Commercial Code article 61 bars every action arising from a contract for the carriage of goods, or from a forwarding (commission) contract for carriage, after one year. The year runs from delivery to the consignee, or from the day delivery should have happened if the goods were totally lost. The record covers debts for 'provision of services' but gives them only the general period (15 years from the due date), with the one-, two- and five-year exceptions of the Civil Code. Nothing in the record asks whether the debt is a carrier's freight charge.

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 of 26 September 1975 (Commercial Code), art. 61, Official Journal 1975 no. 101 of 19 December 1975, page 1311 (bottom of the right column, continued at the top of the left column). Whether a later text changed it was not checked: the amendment ledger does not cover the commercial code.

quoteArabic: «المادة 61 : كل دعوى ناشئة عن عقد نقل الأشياء أو عن عقد العمولة لنقل الأشياء تسقط خلال سنة واحدة. وتسرى هذه المهلة المذكورة في حالة الضياع الكلي ابتداء من اليوم الذي كان يجب فيه تسليم الشيء المنقول وفي جميع الأحوال الأخرى من تاريخ تسليمه للمرسل إليه أو عرضه عليه».
consequence: Example case: a road haulier sues a trading company for freight invoices for goods it delivered 14 months ago. The record would apply the general 15-year limitation and say nothing, but under art. 61 the claim is out of time. The record needs to ask whether the debt arises from a contract for carriage of goods or a forwarding contract. If it does, it should apply the one-year period from delivery to the consignee (art. 61) and warn.

claim: Commercial Code article 245 stays every individual action brought by a member of the body of creditors once a judgment declares the debtor bankrupt or puts it in judicial settlement. Article 246 adds that the judgment makes debts not yet due payable at once. The record leaves this as an open point recalled 'from memory'. It only reaches it through the exit to the specialised commercial court when the lawyer picks the bankruptcy matter. No slot asks whether the defendant is under such a judgment, so an ordinary claim for payment against a bankrupt trader is drafted without warning.

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 (Commercial Code), art. 245 and art. 246, Official Journal 1975 no. 101, page 1331 (bottom of the right column). 1975 wording; I did not check later amendments to Book III (the ledger does not cover the commercial code).

quoteArabic: «المادة 245 : يترتب على الحكم بشهر الافلاس أو التسوية القضائية وقف كل دعوى شخصية لأفراد جماعة الدائنين، وبناء على هذا توقف منذ الحكم كل طرق التنفيذ، سواء على المنقولات أو العقارات من جانب الدائنين الذين لا يضمن ديونهم امتياز خاص أو رهن حيازي أو عقاري على تلك الأموال».
consequence: The record should ask whether the defendant has been declared bankrupt or put in judicial settlement. If so, it should warn that an individual action for payment is stayed (art. 245) and that the creditor's route is through the insolvency proceedings, which the specialised commercial court hears under CPCA 536 مكرر. It should not go on drafting an ordinary claim for the commercial section. Open point o6 can be answered from this text.

claim: Short exchange-law limitations govern a debt embodied in a bill of exchange or a cheque. For a bill of exchange: 3 years from maturity against the acceptor, 1 year from the protest (or from maturity for a bill 'without costs') for the holder against endorsers and drawer, and 6 months between endorsers (art. 461). For a cheque: 6 months from the end of the presentation period for the holder's recourse against endorsers, drawer and other obligors, and 3 years for the holder against the drawee (art. 527). The record's protective reading for o3 is to apply the general period with a reminder. That reading gives a wrong answer whenever the lawyer bases the claim on the instrument itself.

source.what: Ordinance 75-59 (Commercial Code), art. 461 (Official Journal 1975 no. 101, page 1351, right column) and art. 527 (same issue, page 1356, left column). 1975 wording; I did not check later amendments to Book IV (the ledger does not cover the commercial code).

quoteArabic: «المادة 461 : جميع الدعاوى الناشئة عن السفتجة والمرفوعة على قابلها تسقط بمضي ثلاثة أعوام من تاريخ الاستحقاق. وتسقط دعاوى الحامل ضد المظهرين أو الساحب بمضي عام واحد من تاريخ الاحتجاج المحرر في المدة القانونية أو من تاريخ الاستحقاق اذا كانت السفتجة مشتملة على شرط الرجوع بلا مصاريف» ؛ «المادة 527 : تتقادم دعاوى الرجوع بالنسبة لحامل ضد المظهرين أو الساحب أو الملتزمين الآخرين، بمضي ستة أشهر من تاريخ انقضاء مهلة التقديم ... وتتقادم دعوى حامل الشيك على المسحوب عليه بمضي ثلاثة أعوام من تاريخ انقضاء مهلة تقديمه».
consequence: The record should ask whether the claim rests on a bill of exchange or a cheque, and against whom (acceptor, drawer, endorser, drawee). If so, it should apply art. 461 or art. 527 with their starting events, and tell the lawyer that the underlying commercial debt (the general period) is a separate claim. Open point o3 and checklist line k16 can be answered from these texts.

claim: Boundary n1 warns that a trader's claim for things supplied to a non-trader is barred after one year (art. 312). It does not say that when the debtor's acknowledgement interrupts that one-year limitation, the new period is fifteen years (art. 319 ¶2). It also does not say that a short-limitation debt recorded in a written instrument is barred only after fifteen years (art. 313 ¶2, though that paragraph's cross-reference is disputed, see adv-6). A supplier holding a signed statement of account or acknowledgement from a consumer is told the claim may be out of time when it is not.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 (Civil Code), art. 319 ¶2 and art. 313 ¶2, Official Journal 1975 no. 78 of 30 September 1975, page 1008 (art. 313 in the right column, art. 319 in the left column). The store has the same wording (civil-code 319 ¶2, 313 ¶2), and the ledger lists no later amendment.

quoteArabic: «غير أنه اذا حكم بالدين وحاز الحكم قوة الشىء المقضى بــه أو اذا كان الدين يتقادم بسنة وانقطع تقادمه باقرار المدين، كانت مدة التقادم الجديد خمسة عشرة سنة» (المادة 319 الفقرة 2) ؛ «واذا حرر سند بحق من هذه الحقوق فلا يتقادم الحق الا بانقضاء خمسة عشرة سنة» (المادة 313 الفقرة 2).
consequence: When n1 applies, the record should also ask whether the debtor acknowledged the debt after it arose (signed statement, acknowledgement, part payment acknowledged in writing) or whether a written instrument records it. If so, the warning should say that the period is fifteen years from the acknowledgement (art. 319 ¶2), not one year. Without this question the lawyer may give up a claim that is still alive.

claim: n1 tells the lawyer to check the due date, and k13 starts the short periods from the due date. But article 313 ¶1 starts the short limitations it names 'from the time the creditors performed their services, even if they continue to perform others'. On a credit sale, the supply date comes before the due date. The OJ text (Arabic and French alike) refers to 'articles 309 and 311', yet the wording about performed services fits the professionals' and traders' rights of 310 and 312, not periodic rights (309) or taxes (311). So it is unsettled whether the trader-supply year of art. 312 runs from supply or from the due date. The record treats the due date as settled.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 (Civil Code), art. 313 ¶1: Arabic Official Journal 1975 no. 78, page 1008, right column; French edition https://www.joradp.dz/FTP/jo-francais/1975/F1975078.pdf, page 832, right column ('La prescription des créances prévues aux articles 309 et 311, court à partir du jour où les prestations ont été effectuées par les créanciers'). That the cross-reference may be a numbering slip is my own reading (the structure resembles the Egyptian model): treat it as a lead.

quoteArabic: «المادة 313 : يبدأ سريان التقادم فى الحقوق المذكورة فى المادتين 309 و 311 من الوقت الذى يتم فيه الدائنون تقديـم خدماتهم ولو استمروا فى أداء خدمات أخرى».
consequence: For n1, the record should treat the starting point as open (two readings: supply date under art. 313, due date under art. 315). The protective choice is to count from the supply date, the earlier one, and warn on that basis. Example: goods supplied to a non-trader on 1 March 2025 with payment due on 1 September 2025, petition filed on 15 April 2026. Counted from the due date the claim looks in time, but counted from supply the year has run.

claim: Request r5 (price supplement for an excess in quantity) is drafted on the single slot price_supplement_for_excess_quantity. Yet art. 365 ¶2, which b15 quotes, gives the seller a supplement only when the price is fixed per unit and the thing sold is not divisible. Even then the buyer may ask rescission instead if the excess is gross, and the whole rule gives way to a contrary agreement. Most commercial goods sold by quantity (bulk goods, units) are divisible, and in that case the article grants no supplement.

source.what: Ordinance 75-58 (Civil Code), art. 365 ¶2, Official Journal 1975 no. 78, page 1011, left column; the store's civil-code 365 ¶2 has the same wording.

quoteArabic: «وبالعكس إذا تبين أن قدر الشيء المبيع يزيد على ما ذكر بالعقد، وكان الثمن مقدرا بحسب الوحدة وجب على المشتري إذا كان المبيع غير قابل للتقسيم أن يدفع ثمنا زائدا الا إذا كانت الزيادة فاحشة ففي هذه الحالة يجوز له أن يطلب فسخ العقد كل هذا ما لم يوجد اتفاق يخالفه».
consequence: Before drafting r5 on art. 365, the record should ask whether the price was fixed per unit, whether the thing sold is indivisible and whether the contract says otherwise. If the goods are divisible, it should not present art. 365 as the basis for a supplement: the excess quantity is a separate question of delivery and price, outside this article.
